sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module overview and imports
sections.what: Nothing runs here. It describes the debt calculation and loads the helper tools.
sections.why: Gives the reader the formulas before the code.

sections.name: calculate_interest_expense
sections.title: Interest charged on each year's balance
sections.what: Multiplies each year's balance by the interest rate to get that year's interest cost.
sections.why: Interest is a yearly cost that reduces profit.
sections.watch_out: The schedule builder works out its own interest instead of calling this function, so the two can drift apart if one is changed.

sections.name: calculate_debt_schedule
sections.title: Year-by-year debt movements
sections.what: Goes through the years, charging interest on the opening balance, adding new borrowing, subtracting repayments, and carrying the closing balance forward.
sections.why: Keeps debt, interest, and repayments consistent with each other from year to year.
sections.watch_out: The opening balance list it returns is one item shorter than the other lists.

sections.name: calculate_debt_auto
sections.title: Repayments as a share of debt
sections.what: Sets each year's repayment as a fixed share of the opening balance, then builds the borrowing and repayment lists and passes them to the schedule builder.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user express repayment as a rule instead of typing in amounts.
sections.watch_out: It works out its own balance list and then discards it, so only the repayment amounts it produces affect the result.

summary: Tracks how much the company owes each year, the interest it pays, and how new borrowing and repayments change the balance.
purpose: Produces interest expense and the debt balance for each year, for use in the income statement and balance sheet.
why: Interest reduces profit and debt appears on the balance sheet, so the model needs a yearly debt schedule.
how: 1. Start with the opening debt. 2. Each year, charge interest on the opening balance. 3. Add new borrowing and subtract repayments to get the closing balance. 4. Carry the closing balance into the next year. The automatic version first works out repayments as a share of the balance.
inputs: Starting debt; annual interest rate; lists of new borrowing and repayments by year; number of years. The automatic version takes a repayment rate and an optional list of new borrowing instead of a repayment list.
outputs: Interest expense per year, opening balance per year, closing balance per year, and the borrowing and repayment lists.
risks: The opening balance list comes out one item shorter than the other lists, which can cause mismatched years. Repayments are expected as positive numbers, but the cash flow code describes them as negative. Interest uses the opening balance, so new borrowing in a year does not add interest in that year.
debug: When results look shifted by a year, check the length of the opening balance list. If cash flow looks wrong, confirm repayments are entered as positive numbers. Check interest by multiplying the opening balance by the rate.
